subject.title: fix(gateway): force exit on zombie shutdown + 503 healthz during shutdown

question: Should Gateway supervised recovery adopt this default 5s post-clean-shutdown `process.exit(0)` watchdog plus strict internal `/healthz?strict=1` preflight semantics?
rationale: The code appears correct and well-tested, but this changes operator-facing shutdown and recovery behavior in a way automation should not decide without owner intent.

options.title: Accept Guarded Recovery Contract
options.body: Merge after a Gateway owner confirms the default forced-exit watchdog, strict internal probe, and env timeout are the desired supervised-recovery contract.

options.title: Narrow Before Merge
options.body: Require the watchdog to become opt-in, longer-timeout, or otherwise less aggressive if owners do not want clean shutdowns to force process exit by default.

options.title: Pause For Architecture Choice
options.body: Pause or close if owners prefer solving this through supervisor/install behavior or the original SIGKILL root cause instead of a runtime watchdog.

recommendation.title: Accept Guarded Recovery Contract
recommendation.body: Merge after a Gateway owner confirms the default forced-exit watchdog, strict internal probe, and env timeout are the desired supervised-recovery contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter appears in recent Gateway lifecycle path history and is the strongest available owner signal for the operator-sensitive shutdown contract.
